title: Chapter 25
content:
Just before the laborers' van pulled out onto the main thoroughfare, it slowed to a momentary halt. Seizing the split-second window, Jakyeong dropped from the undercarriage, hit the asphalt, and rolled clear.

He slipped into the dense brush alongside the road like a shadow, holding his breath until the rumble of the diesel engine faded into the distance. Once he was completely alone, he pushed himself to his feet.

Brushing away the twigs and dirt clinging to his clothes, he glanced back over his shoulder. Kang Il-hyun’s fortress had vanished entirely, hidden behind the rolling crest of the hills.

Jakyeong rolled his shoulders, working the stiffness from his joints, then retrieved his cap and mask from his pocket to obscure his face. Emerging onto the main road, he spotted a taxi idling outside a convenience store—the cab he’d ordered through a burner app.

He slid into the back seat. The driver glanced into the rearview mirror. "You call for the cab?"

"Yes. Take me to this address."

The cabbie checked the navigation route and shifted into drive. After about an hour's drive leaving the capital far behind, the taxi pulled up outside an auto repair shop nestled in a quiet, rural corner of Gyeonggi Province.

Jakyeong paid the fare in cash, stepped out, and strode toward the garage. A mechanic in the middle of talking to a customer stepped in his path, eyeing the masked, hooded visitor with immediate suspicion.

"Can I help you?"

"I'm here to see the owner. Tell him Han sent me; he'll know."

The mechanic hesitated, muttered for him to wait, and disappeared into the back office. Moments later, a burly, broad-shouldered man emerged. He wore an eye-searing, brightly patterned short-sleeve shirt stretched so tight across his massive chest that the seams looked ready to pop.

The man recognized Jakyeong in an instant, crossing the distance in heavy strides and wrapping him in an aggressive bear hug.

"Look at you! How many years has it been?!"

Jakyeong tapped the boulder-like arm practically crushing his windpipe. "Can't... breathe. Let go."

The owner laughed, releasing him before shooting his employee a look that told him to clear out. Once the shop floor was empty, Jakyeong pulled off his cap and lowered the mask.

Wang Ryun was Wang Han's younger cousin. He ran an auto repair shop now as a legitimate front, but he used to broker heavy black-market arms. Jakyeong hadn't seen him since he was eighteen—a reunion seven years in the making.

"How've you been holding up?" Ryun asked, clapping him on the shoulder.

"Same as always. You haven't changed a bit either," Jakyeong said. "Look, I know our agreed drop date is still a ways out, but I'm here early."

Ryun’s jovial expression tightened into a frown. "Did something go sideways?"

"No. Just have a personal errand to take care of today."

Ryun gave a slow nod, knowing better than to press for details. He turned and guided Jakyeong behind the main office into a cluttered tool storage bay stacked high with grease-stained parts and wooden crates.

Clearing away a tower of cardboard boxes stacked shoulder-high, a heavy steel trapdoor was revealed. Ryun popped open a fist-sized padlock and led the way down into an underground storage cellar crammed with industrial salvage.

Kneeling on the floor, Ryun peeled back a sheet of yellow vinyl linoleum to expose a set of wooden floorboards. Beneath them sat several matte-black tactical cases.

Ryun hauled them up one by one, the heavy steel thudding against the concrete. Three cases in total.

He flipped the latches on the first crate and shoved it toward Jakyeong. "Take a look."

Resting in custom-cut foam were two semi-automatic pistols chambered for 17-round magazines.

The second crate held spare magazines, fragmentation grenades, smoke canisters, and tactical C4 breaching charges.

And inside the third and final case... a high-precision, long-range sniper rifle.

"Well? Will she do the job?" Ryun asked.

"Immaculate," Jakyeong murmured, running a gloved finger along the cold, matte-black finish of the rifle chassis.

This was the instrument designated to end Kang Il-hyun’s life. In contract sniping, precision fire was typically categorized into three terminal zones: the limbs, the center of mass (the heart), and the brain stem. Unlike a severed femoral artery or a punctured ventricle, a direct headshot severed consciousness before the target even registered they were dying.

The client’s explicit requirement had been the heart.

A bullet through the chest meant Kang Il-hyun would cling to life for roughly sixty agonized seconds before suffocating in his own blood. What kind of face will he make when death stares him down? Will he still be able to crack slick jokes with a hole in his chest?

Jakyeong almost regretted that he wouldn't be close enough to witness it.

He stepped into the back room, stripped down, and geared up. He threw on dark, flexible tactical attire, holstered the combat knives and sidearms, and strapped a modular ammo rig around his waist. He packed the fragmentation grenades, smoke canisters, and breaching charges into a compact tactical sling bag.

When he emerged, Ryun led him to the rear lot beside the garage. Tugging away a heavy black tarp, a sleek motorcycle was revealed: a late-model Kawasaki sports bike fitted with cloned, untraceable plates.

Jakyeong wheeled the bike out into the sunlight. He strapped on a matte-black full-face helmet and kicked the ignition. The engine turned over with a deep, feral purr.

Ryun stepped up beside him. "Watch your back out there."

Jakyeong gave a firm nod, revving the throttle. The aggressive rumble of the exhaust set a familiar thrill humming through his veins—it had been far too long since he’d ridden.

Mounted to the handlebars was a ruggedized smartphone displaying the active GPS feed. The red blip was currently in transit, crawling along a southern arterial road.

"See you soon," Jakyeong said.

With a brief wave, he dumped the clutch, and the Kawasaki roared onto the asphalt, tearing into traffic. He wove effortlessly between lanes, cutting through congested bottlenecks like a scalpel. As the speedometer climbed, city blocks and passenger sedans blurred into static. The raw velocity kicked his adrenaline into high gear.

The distance between his bike and the tracking beacon narrowed rapidly.

Closing in on the target coordinates, he spotted a vehicle idling at a four-way intersection up ahead, waiting for the light to change. The white sports car was unmistakable.

The signal turned green, the sports car pulled away, and Jakyeong tucked into its blind spot, shadowing its rear bumper.

Pulling up flush against the driver's side door, Jakyeong glanced down. The tinted window glided down, and a snarling face poked out, screaming at him to back off.

It wasn't Choi Ki-tae. A rough-looking enforcer was behind the wheel, spewing venomous curses.

Jakyeong pinned the throttle, surged forward, and executed a sharp, aggressive sweep across the sports car's front bumper, cutting it off inches from its grille.

Startled, the driver slammed the brakes, the car fish-tailing as tires shrieked against the asphalt, laying down thick black skid marks.

Glancing back over his shoulder, Jakyeong raised his left hand and slowly, deliberately flashed his middle finger.

Enraged, the sports car gunned its engine with a deafening roar and tore after him in hot pursuit.

"To what do I owe the pleasure?"

Seeing his secretary's nervous, pale face earlier, Kang Il-hyun had already deduced who had dropped by unannounced.

Kim Sun-young—who had been staring down at the polished acrylic desk plaque reading Managing Director Kang Il-hyun—turned around with agonizing slowness. Unlike her subdued appearance at the family dinner, her makeup was stark and heavy, draped in designer silks.

She took a seat on the leather lounge sofa. Il-hyun slipped off his suit jacket, draped it over his valet stand, and reached for the desk intercom to order refreshments.

"Don't bother with tea," she cut in sharply. "It's not as if you and I share the kind of affectionate relationship where we sit and sip tea together, is it?"

"Fair enough," Il-hyun said smoothly, sinking into the armchair across from her. "Let's skip the pleasantries. What brings you here?"

"What the hell do you think you're playing at?"

"You'll have to be more specific, Mother."

"Why did you lay a hand on President Choi? Do you have any idea who that man is to me?"

Il-hyun produced a silver cigarette case, placed a smoke between his lips, and sparked the tip. Leaning back comfortably, he exhaled a slow plume of gray smoke.

Under interrogation, Choi had broken easily, confessing that the untraceable cash transfer had been made under Kim Sun-young’s explicit instructions—claiming he had no knowledge of the end goal, only that he was doing his cousin a favor.

Since the street fixers who received the deposit had gone to ground, forensic confirmation of the hit contract remained elusive. But Tae-soo’s men were already scouring the city; finding them was merely a matter of time. And once they were dragged before him, Il-hyun intended to tear them apart limb from limb.

"I could ask you the same question, Mother," Il-hyun drawled. "What exactly were you plotting?"

"What?"

"Please, don't harbor so much resentment toward me. I'm actually quite fond of you."

Sun-young scoffed in disbelief. The claim was laughable.

Sure enough, Il-hyun’s follow-up was drenched in acid.

"You're greedy, ruthless, and utterly treacherous. In many ways, you and I are cut from the exact same cloth. Birds of a feather, as they say. If only Seok-joo had inherited your venom, I might have found him somewhat tolerable."

Veins popped along the back of Sun-young’s hand as her grip tightened around her designer clutch. "Is that any way to speak to an elder?"

"If my candor offended you, I offer my deepest apologies."

"You certainly have a talent for dispensing hollow apologies."

Il-hyun ground his cigarette into the glass ashtray, crossing his arms with a pleasant smile.

There had been a brief, foolish window in his childhood when he had actively sought her affection. Having never known a mother's warmth, he had tried to earn the favor of the new matriarch when she first entered the house—only to be met with frigid contempt.

He hadn't taken it to heart. That was simply how the world turned. From her perspective, an illegitimate stepson from another woman's womb was an eyesore. Besides, even as a boy, Il-hyun was never the type of child anyone could find endearing.

His methods of seeking attention had been so profoundly twisted that Chairman Kang had contemplated institutionalizing his second son on multiple occasions. It was the sole reason the Chairman had pulled high-level strings to secure Il-hyun a medical exemption from military service under the guise of 'severe mental instability.'

In reality, the old man had simply been terrified that if Il-hyun were handed a loaded rifle in the barracks, he would start shooting his comrades for sport.

"I'll offer you one opportunity," Il-hyun murmured, his tone dropping an octave. "Unless your cleanup is immaculate... confess now."

"I have no earthly idea what you're babbling about."

"Don't play this game with me, Mother. When I pull the truth into the light... how do you plan to survive the fallout?"

Sun-young tilted her chin, offering a confident, mocking smile. She told him to go ahead and try.

She was certain Il-hyun wouldn't find a single shred of physical evidence linking her to the morning's sniper attack. Her fixers had caught wind of the loose ends and permanently scrubbed the mercenary safehouse earlier today. Furthermore, her contacts had already leaked whispers of the assault on Jang Yi-an directly to the Triad leadership in Hong Kong.

Sun-young rose to her feet. Il-hyun tilted his head up, his dark eyes locking onto her face.

"Mother... do you remember the golden rule of our household?"

Sun-young said nothing.

"Under no circumstances does family inflict physical harm upon family."

Sun-young let out a dry, contemptuous laugh. "Is that why you drove an ice pick into Seok-joo’s head?"

The polite curve of Il-hyun's lips evaporated instantly, leaving behind a chilling void.

"Clause two: Any member who inflicts bodily harm shall submit entirely to the judgment and retaliation of the victim, without interference from the rest of the bloodline."

Sun-young looked down at him, utterly incredulous. "So you're saying that if I put a bullet in you, it falls within house rules?"

"Not quite," Il-hyun whispered, a lethal glint flashing in his eyes. "It means that if I'm to be killed... Seok-joo is the only one with the right to attempt it."

"Spare me your word games. You can scream all you want, but I know nothing of your little drama."

Sun-young turned toward the door with an air of absolute composure, but inside, a cold tremor of dread was steadily taking root.

Kang Il-hyun had been an expert in psychological cruelty since he was in diapers. Seeing that unblinking, feral predator look up at her from behind the desk set her teeth on edge.

Before he tears my throat out, I have to cut his legs out from under him.

If she allowed Kang Il-hyun to claim the Chairman's throne at the upcoming inauguration, she and Seok-joo would be the very first corpses thrown to the dogs.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Mandatory Military Exemption (군대 면제 / 심신미약): In South Korea, all able-bodied men are subject to mandatory military conscription. Exemptions on the grounds of "mental and physical infirmity" (simsin-miyak) are notoriously rare and heavily scrutinized. Chairman Kang fabricating or leveraging extreme psychological evaluations to keep a volatile, sociopathic Il-hyun away from military firearms reflects both high-level corruption and the family's terrifying internal dynamics.

  • Green is the Same Color (초록은 동색): A Korean idiom equivalent to "birds of a feather flock together" or "two peas in a pod," used here by Il-hyun to mockingly point out that he and his stepmother share the exact same predatory, calculating nature.
